issue: Business logic (price calculation) missing — controller trusts client-supplied prices
evidence: itemsPrice, taxPrice, shippingPrice, totalPrice accepted from req.body without server-side recalculation
recommendation: Extract price calculation to a service/utility layer that recalculates from DB product prices.

issue: Route handler contains full business logic — file I/O, validation, error handling all inline
layer: Route → should delegate to Controller → Service
evidence: ~100 lines of fs.readFile/writeFile, JSON parse, validation, response formatting all inside route callbacks
recommendation: Extract to featureFlagsController.js following existing controller pattern. Move file I/O to a service/repository layer.

issue: MCP server writes directly to backend/features.json — cross-boundary file coupling
evidence: FEATURES_PATH = ROOT / 'backend' / 'features.json' — Python process writes file that Node.js process reads
recommendation: MCP server should call backend API (POST /api/feature-flags/state) instead of writing files directly. Or use a shared database.

issue: No service layer — controllers call Mongoose models directly
evidence: All 3 controllers (user, product, order) import models and call Model.find/create/findById directly
recommendation: For a legacy project this is acceptable but documented as tech debt. Critical business logic (pricing, auth) should move to services first.

issue: Review creation tightly coupled to product document — embedded subdocument pattern limits scalability
evidence: Reviews stored as embedded array in Product document. No separate Review model.
recommendation: For current scale this works. At scale (1000+ reviews/product), consider separate Review collection with product reference.

issue: Password hashing logic coupled to Mongoose model pre-save hook
evidence: userSchema.pre('save', async function...) — bcrypt hashing in model hook
recommendation: Acceptable pattern for this project size. Note: makes unit testing harder since hashing runs on every save.

issue: No input validation layer — controllers validate inline (or don't validate at all)
evidence: No express-validator or joi middleware. Controllers trust req.body shape.
recommendation: Add validation middleware (express-validator) between routes and controllers for request body/params/query validation.

issue: Feature flags route breaks controller pattern — logic inline in route file
evidence: All other routes (user, product, order, upload) delegate to controllers. Feature flags routes contain all logic inline.
recommendation: Create featureFlagsController.js to match existing pattern.

issue: Feature flags mutation routes missing auth middleware — inconsistent with all other mutation endpoints
evidence: POST /state and /traffic have no protect/admin. All other POST/PUT/DELETE routes use protect middleware.
recommendation: Add protect + admin middleware to match pattern of other routes.

evidence: Some controllers: res.status(404); throw new Error(). Others: res.status(404).json({ message }). No consistent pattern.
recommendation: Standardize on throw new Error() pattern with express-async-handler catching and forwarding to errorMiddleware.

issue: RAG config hardcodes model names and Qdrant URL — no configuration injection
recommendation: Already uses dataclass defaults which can be overridden. Consider environment variable support for deployment flexibility.
